# RuleReceipt

> RuleReceipt checks what your AI coding agent actually did in a session against
> your own written rules (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules) and marks each rule
> followed, broken, or can't-tell — with the exact line as proof. It runs locally;
> plain `rulereceipt check` makes zero network calls. It detects and reports, and
> blocks only a narrow opt-in file/branch subset; it does not make the model obey.

## What it is
- A command-line tool: `npx rulereceipt check` reads the finished session transcript and reports per rule.
- Supported agents (read sessions): Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, Antigravity, OpenCode, Cline, Devin. Any other agent is experimental.
- Supported OS: macOS and Linux. Windows is untested.
- Verdicts: followed / not followed (with the quoted evidence) / couldn't tell / rule not visible (edited a covered file with no record the rule was loaded) / needs human judgment. An `--llm` grade is a labelled opinion only and never fails CI or blocks.

## Key pages
- Home: https://rulereceipt.dev
- Accuracy (real measured false-FAIL numbers): https://rulereceipt.dev/accuracy
- Blog: https://rulereceipt.dev/blog
- Check your rules file in the browser: https://rulereceipt.dev/check
- Source (free CLI, source-available): https://github.com/rulereceipt/rulereceipt
- Security policy: https://rulereceipt.dev/.well-known/security.txt

## Privacy
- The CLI runs on your machine and uploads nothing by default. Three opt-ins (`--llm`, `--share`, telemetry) are off unless you ask.
- The website uses PostHog analytics; see the privacy policy at https://rulereceipt.dev/privacy
